title: How much does it cost to save a life?
html:
In 2006 two hedge fund analysts, Holden Karnofsky and Elie Hassenfeld, tried to find out which charities do the most good per dollar. They expected clear answers. Most charities couldn’t say what their programmes achieved, let alone at what cost, so the two quit their jobs and founded GiveWell to find out.

They found that some health programmes in low-income countries save a life for roughly $3,000–5,000, while others aimed at similar problems cost hundreds of times more. Most donors had no way of telling them apart.

Read: Peter Singer, “How much does it cost to save a life, and how can you find which charities do it best?”, chapter 6 of The Life You Can Save (free download) (20 mins).
